A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ControlAudio paper, including Appendices A-E. All 18 pages are readable. Pages 2-18 have identical extracted text and rendered images; first-page differences concern corresponding-author information and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original ControlAudio experiments on temporal control, speech intelligibility, and general text-to-audio generation, including objective and subjective results and ablations in Tables 1-5.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original ControlAudio evaluations, subjective studies, and ablation results in Tables 1-5.

M1.justification: The data-construction pipelines, structured prompts, unified text encoder, three-stage training, progressive sampling, and appendix LLM planner are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training coverage in Appendix A is identical. Both versions evaluate the same tasks using AudioCondition, AC-Filtered, AudioCaps, LibriTTS-R, and LibriSpeech, with no added or removed scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments in Tables 1-5, including the AudioLDM, AudioComposer, FreeAudio, VoiceLDM, and VoiceDiT comparisons.

E3.justification: Splits, preprocessing, model configurations, metrics, and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 20-person subjective evaluation and the 100-step sampling analysis with transition timestep 88.

E4.justification: The prompt-format and vocabulary-granularity ablations, sampling-guidance analysis in Figure 3, and planning examples in Appendix D are identical.

E5.justification: Experimental tables retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and no seed or run-count information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, ControlAudio retains Eb 55.58 and At 79.52 in Table 1 and WER 6.84 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(6) and the mathematical definitions in Appendix D are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about unified timing-controlled and intelligible audio generation, progressive modeling, and state-of-the-art temporal accuracy and speech clarity.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are identical. The limitations concerning stylistic control, audio-quality versus intelligibility tradeoffs, and annotated-data scarcity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A-E retain identical preprocessing, architecture, optimizer, evaluation, planning, and transcription details. The demo link is unchanged; the correspondence-footnote edit does not alter technical or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to temporal-control methods and speech-generation systems is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author marker to Zehua Chen and replaces the correspondence email footnote with 'Corresponding Authors: Zehua Chen and Jun Zhu.' The arXiv version/date stamp also changes. Body wording and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-8 retain identical formatting, captions, and placement. Pages 2-18 render identically, and the first-page attribution edits preserve the existing layout.

improvement.justification: The revision changes corresponding-author information and version metadata only. Scientific arguments, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, limitations, and substantive presentation remain identical, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
